metadata.title: The next matching level for triangle-free graphs with bounded degree and an exact Bougard-Joret value
metadata.description:
Let T(d, m) be the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph with maximum degree at most d and matching number at most m. We prove T(d, d + 1) = d² + d + 2 for every integer d ≥ 7. A shortest-odd-cycle deficit bound and a five-type equality obstruction give the maximum on 2d + 3 vertices; the Tutte-Berge formula extends it to every order. The attaining construction is due to Banak, Ekim and Taşkın; the contribution is the uniform upper bound. It resolves the published bounds 184 ≤ T(13, 14) ≤ 185 in favor of 184, and it gives a computation-free proof that d + 1 < Z(d) for every d ≥ 7, which places the level m = d + 1 inside the range d < m < Z(d) of the Ahanjideh-Ekim-Yıldız conjecture.

As a consequence the Bougard-Joret function satisfies f(2d + 3, 2, d + 2) = d² + 4d + 2 for every d ≥ 7, so the first line ⌈nk/2⌉ of their conjecture fails by ⌊d/2⌋ - 1 at these parameters, an unbounded amount; the lower value is excluded because every extremal triangle-free graph on 2d + 3 vertices has two vertices with the same d neighbours. Exact computations support the proofs without replacing them: 48 saved graphs pass two independent implementations, and no five-type tuple survives (287,564 tuples for d = 7, ..., 30 in the main run, 17,040 compositions for d = 7, ..., 10 in the independent audit). A configuration-split satisfiability search finds no counterexample at d = 7 and d = 8 (one d = 8 configuration reached its limit and is excluded by an identity). The full Ahanjideh-Ekim-Yıldız conjecture remains open.

Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/combinatorics/bougard-joret).
metadata.version_notes: Adds a prior-work section that defines the Ahanjideh-Ekim-Yıldız threshold Z(d) exactly and gives a computation-free proof of d + 1 < Z(d) for every d ≥ 7 (for d = 7, 9, 11 it was known only from the integer-programming values of Banak, Ekim and Taşkın), a computations section with the four algorithms (five-type enumeration, certificate checks, independent audit, configuration-split satisfiability search) with commands, versions where recorded, run times and hashes, results tables and figures generated from the archived artifacts, a validation section that reports the unfinished global search, an ablation, the proof edits (the sum step in the case q = p, renamed symbols) and the current second-regime paper. The theorems T(d, d + 1) = d² + d + 2 and f(2d + 3, 2, d + 2) = d² + 4d + 2 are unchanged.
